title: The Library of Celsus Facade
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Hover over nine numbered parts of the Library of Celsus at Ephesus, from the steps to the burial chamber under the floor, to learn what is original, what was reassembled, and what the building was for, then test yourself in Quiz mode.

educational.topic: The Library of Celsus at Ephesus
learningObjectives: The learner will read the front of the Library of Celsus part by part: say which parts are original design, which are copies or reconstruction, and what the building was for, a public library built as a son's memorial and a tomb.
prerequisites: Curetes Street, Hadrian, and the classical orders, from [Chapter 10](../../chapters/10-ephesus-greco-roman-city/index.md).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Interactive exploration followed by retrieval practice
keyQuestions: What is original, and what was reassembled?
commonMisconceptions: It is a ruin that has never been touched.
assessmentOpportunities: Quiz mode: identify each marked part from its description

controls.name: Explore
controls.description: Default mode: hover a marker or label to read about that part.

controls.name: Quiz
controls.description: Hides the labels and asks you to click the marker that matches each description.
